description: The Signature SSD Sentinel is Manon's original drive-steward design: one calm dashboard that predicts failure weeks ahead instead of merely reporting today's health. Every number it shows is paired with the action it implies, so a drive is never a mystery.

title: Signature SSD Sentinel — Sentinel install ritual

title: Signature SSD Sentinel — Sentinel dashboard

title: Signature SSD Sentinel — Predictive wear model
description: Instead of echoing today's S.M.A.R.T. values, Sentinel fits a wear-rate line through the drive's own history and projects the date each attribute crosses its threshold. A drive at 94 percent with a steep slope gets flagged sooner than one at 88 percent that has been flat for a year.

title: Signature SSD Sentinel — Sentinel benchmark lab
description: The benchmark lab runs sequential and random tests at three fill levels, because an SSD's numbers change as it fills. Reporting all three stops the classic trick of quoting empty-drive speeds for a drive that will live at 90 percent full.

title: Signature SSD Sentinel — Adaptive over-provisioning
description: Sentinel sizes the spare area from the drive's actual write pattern instead of a fixed 10 percent: write-heavy workloads get more, read-heavy archives get less. The slider still exists for purists, but the adaptive default is right more often.

title: Signature SSD Sentinel — Deep scan
description: The deep scan walks every block including the spare area map the controller will admit to, and logs the result against the baseline snapshot. Any block that moved since baseline gets named in the report, not just counted.

title: Signature SSD Sentinel — Forensic erase
description: Forensic erase performs the cryptographic discard and then verifies it by sampling blocks across the whole NAND, reporting a signed certificate of destruction. It is the erase you hand to an auditor, not just to a buyer.

title: Signature SSD Sentinel — Migration engine
description: The migration engine clones with bad-block awareness: it reads around weak blocks, retries with smaller chunks, and tells you exactly which files were affected. A migration report lists every byte that did not survive, which a blind clone never does.
